title: U.S. Measles Cases Pass 5,000 for First Time Since 1991 as Elimination Status Faces Review

content:
Measles cases in the United States have passed 5,000 in a single year for the first time since 1991, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported — and next week, an international panel will decide whether the country keeps the measles-free status it has held since 2000.

The CDC counted 5,182 confirmed cases as of Nov. 5, according to its update issued Nov. 6, with 330 new infections in the latest week alone. The outbreak has spread across 47 jurisdictions, with 43 outbreaks reported so far in 2026. About 96% of this year's cases have been in people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown. The CDC reports 562 people hospitalized — about 11% of cases.

A disputed death count

How many people measles has killed this year is now a matter of public dispute. The CDC's national tally lists four measles-associated deaths in 2026. State health departments, however, have reported at least eight deaths linked to the disease, including six in Pennsylvania, one in New York and one in Wisconsin, with very young children among them, according to USA Today and Reuters reporting.

The gap arose after the CDC, under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., switched from state health departments' figures to mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics to track measles deaths. The CDC says it is working with the U.S. Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to settle on a standard definition for a measles death.

The Nov. 10 review

Measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, meaning the virus no longer spread on its own inside the country year-round. That status is now at risk.

The Pan American Health Organization's Measles and Rubella Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission meets Nov. 10–13 to review countries' elimination status. The U.S. and Mexico reviews were moved to the regular November meeting because U.S. authorities were still carrying out analysis, including complete viral genome sequencing.

The decision rests on genetics, not on how many people get sick. PAHO defines re-established endemic transmission as uninterrupted circulation of the same virus genotype and lineage for 12 months or more in a specific geographic area. For the United States, the analysis period starts Jan. 20, 2025, when the West Texas outbreak began. Experts cited in June argued that continuous transmission since that outbreak meets the 12-month definition — but as of Nov. 7, no formal determination exists.

The Americas region already lost its measles elimination status in November 2025, after Canada experienced continuous transmission for at least 12 months.

What it means for the border

The West Texas outbreak that started the clock is the closest measles epicenter to Laredo, and the coming review covers Mexico as well as the United States. Public health agencies point to vaccination — the MMR vaccine — as the main defense against a disease that spreads through the air and can linger in a room after an infected person leaves.
